title: Immediate information gain and total identification cost differ
problem: R39 asks whether experiment value can be computed before choosing a separating question.
failure: A uniquely balanced initial binary question can cost more over the complete identification tree even with uniform hypothesis probabilities and equal test costs.
correction: For a fixed finite distinguishable hypothesis set, minimize unnormalized cost D(S)=min_T[c(T)W(S)+D(S intersect T)+D(S minus T)]. The eight-hypothesis example has expected cost 13/4 if the balanced test is forced first versus 25/8 globally. Exact finite controls compare the recurrence with exhaustive trees.
transfer: Evaluate immediate information gain, future available experiments and complete expected cost separately. Preserve unmodeled possibilities and avoid assuming that the finite candidate set contains the truth.
limits: Known finite hypothesis set, positive weights and costs, noiseless deterministic binary tests, no state change. 96 test families, 15552 weighted/cost cases, 388800 tree evaluations. Classical optimal decision-tree problem. No novelty, empirical cognitive or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
